title: Wide research: user entry point, honest estimate and spend gate, per-item retry, replay after reload
summary: Give the existing subagent.research_fan_out engine a product surface. Add a 'Bred forskning' control with item-count presets, a start card that states the expected scale before anything is spawned (items x rounds x minutes, plus cost on metered routes), a status grid of per-item cards with retry for failed or refused items, a mid-run progress and spend check after the first N items (Continue or Wrap up now), and durable per-item results so the grid survives a reload. Under ZDR the grid stays live-only.
whyItMatters: Wide research is Manus's signature feature and serves Verevon's B2B lists (suppliers, competitors, leads). The engine is already paid for; without an entry point, a cost statement and retry it is unusable and unsafe, and a cost gate fits Verevon's honest-cost stance.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (manus-product-ux-038 SRC UX, web-manus-web-product-023 DOC architecture)
others: Manus web (DOC): plan limits on concurrency and task count
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Controller decomposes into independent items -> estimate a cost range from per-item budget x item count -> start card with Start or 'Always auto-start' -> spawn up to K concurrent isolated sub-runs, each in its own context -> stream per-item status into a 3-column grid with replay link and retry -> after the first N items compute actual spend and show a Skip or Continue card -> 'Wrap up now' -> controller merges structured per-item results. Sub-agents never talk to each other.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: SRC: engine exists (one tool call, N parallel items, structured per-item results merged in order, kill switch WIDE_RESEARCH_FAN_OUT_ENABLED, default concurrency 4) and live cards by batchId exist. Missing: a composer entry point (planned C6), a pre-run estimate and accept gate, a mid-run spend check, per-item retry, durable replay (cards come back empty after reload, planned C7), and scale (default 4 rounds and 2 subagents on the subscription route; 12/24/48 presets wait on owner decision OD7). Do mode only. DOC: on the subscription route cost-core meters nothing (CostBasis::Subscription), so a USD budget is a no-op there.

approachOriginal: Model Plane execution-core: add an estimate step before spawning that is computed from item count, round budget and observed per-item p50 time, and expressed in items, rounds and minutes (USD only when the route is metered, via a run-scoped cost-core check such as the planned cost_guard.rs). Emit an awaiting-approval style start card that the user can set to 'always auto-start', and after the first N completed items emit a progress and spend card with Continue or Wrap up now. Persist the batch and per-item results in session-core so replay works after reload, and add a retry action per item that re-spawns only that child (research-only toolset, C8). Long batches run through the existing WideResearch Temporal workflow (apps/Model Plane/go/services/orchestrator-core/cmd/workflows/wide_research.go). Frontend: 'Bred forskning' control, estimate card, grid with retry, spend card. Under ZDR skip persistence and degrade to a live-only grid.
risks: Spend blowouts and provider rate limits at scale. OD7 recommends no confirm gate in v1; the estimate card should therefore default to informational for small runs and gate only above an org-set size. Credential lifetime caps wide research at about 6 to 8 items on Terra without C9. ZDR forbids durable replay.

alreadyPlanned.where: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md rows C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C9 and decision OD7 (line 447); apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/chat-wave2-specs-2026-09-28/wide-research.md section 2.2 (cost_guard.rs). The estimate card, mid-run spend check and per-item retry are not in the plan.

verevon.exactGap: The engine exists: execution-core spawn_research_fan_out runs N delegated Researcher children behind a semaphore (default 4, cap 16, kill switch WIDE_RESEARCH_FAN_OUT_ENABLED), refuses items past the child ceiling per item, merges results in order, and ChatWideResearchPanel shows live cards by batchId inside the live run rail (the Agent Run Console lists them in its timeline). Missing: a composer entry point (plan C6), any start card or pre-run estimate, a mid-run spend check, per-item retry, and replay after reload (the panel states it only knows what it watched; plan C7). execution-core has no cost-core client and cost_guard.rs does not exist, and a USD gate is a no-op on the Subscription route.
reuse: spawn_research_fan_out with FanOutItemResult::refused/failed/ok as the per-item status source
session-core subagent edge metadata (goal_summary, batch_id) plus the lineage read already used by RunPlanPanel for grid replay
RunDeadline in run_budget.rs (wall clock and credential guard) for the minutes estimate
cost-core GET /api/v1/cost/run (ledger GetRunUsage) for a run-scoped spend read on metered routes
ChatWideResearchPanel status vocabulary and card grid
plan rows C3 to C10 and decision OD7 rather than restating them
verevon.constraints: Children run under delegated bearers (300 s default), so scale on the subscription route is credential-bound until C9 or OD8; the org cap (max_subagents_per_run) must clamp a client-requested item count server-side (client asks, server clamps, C5). Children must stay research-only (C8) and inherit the parent authority; nothing here may widen it. ZDR: no lineage-based replay, grid stays live-only. goal_summary is truncated to 200 characters, so a retry cannot rely on it. The Go WideResearchWorkflow is not a usable long-batch host: it takes plain query strings, hardcodes run ids research-branch-N, thread wide-research and 5 turns, passes only OrgID and UserID (no delegated child lineage or per-item authority), and capability-core only lets a scoped scheduled fire start the default supervision workflow.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Remove "long batches run through the existing WideResearch Temporal workflow": it is a pre-governance step loop and cannot be fired from a scoped schedule (workflow_dispatcher.go:227-233). Scale through the in-loop engine and plan rows C3 to C5 and C9. The estimate card should be informational on the Subscription route (items x rounds x minutes from RunDeadline and observed per-item time) and show USD only on metered routes through a new run-scoped check (execution-core needs a cost-core client; budget/check needs run_id). Retry means re-spawning one child with the original item text, so store the full item goal or re-read the parent tool input. Replay should rebuild the grid from lineage edges (batch_id, goal_summary) plus child run status; per-item answers are plan C7.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the whole feature, but plan rows C3 to C10 already own entry point, limits, replay and credential work; the new delta in this item (estimate card, mid-run spend check, per-item retry) is M.
verevon.verdictReason: Most of the feature is already planned and the engine is built; the item should cite the plan rows, carry only the estimate, spend check and retry delta, and drop the unsuitable Temporal workflow step.

title: Persistent goals with a token budget, a completion judge and auto-continuation
summary: Add a Goal record in session-core {objective, success_criteria, token_budget, used, status active|completed|blocked|cancelled} and a continuation driver, hosted as a Temporal workflow in orchestrator-core, that starts budgeted Do runs until a cheap judge model (verevon-balance) confirms the criteria with evidence, or a budget or blocker is hit, then notifies the user. The Agent Run Console's goal launcher is the natural UI host, with a goal bar showing budget used and compare-and-set edits.
whyItMatters: Outcome agents that work for a long time are the core of the Manus and ChatGPT Work vision, and goals are present in 6 of 12 references. Verevon has no goal primitive, and long autonomous work is also capped by the 300 s delegated bearer and a default of 4 rounds, so a user cannot hand over a multi-step objective and come back to a result.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Codex (persisted ThreadGoal with token budget and an audited completion check)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Goal{objective, success_criteria, token_budget, used, status}. When the run goes idle, a continuation driver re-prompts with the goal state; a cheap judge checks completion against the criteria with evidence; stop on budget exhaustion or a blocker and notify. Completion is audited, not self-declared by the worker model.

evidence: grep of apps/Model Plane/rust/services/*.rs for ThreadGoal, thread_goal, LoopGuard: no matches
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/runtime_loop/agent.rs:24 ('goal' is only the run's bound task string)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/agents/components/AgentRunConsole.tsx:168-330 (goal launcher UI that could host a goal bar)

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: No durable goal, budget accounting, completion judge or continuation driver. A Do run ends when its rounds end, and delegated authority lapses after 300 s.

approachOriginal: Model Plane. Goal rows and budget accounting in session-core; a GoalContinuation workflow in orchestrator-core that starts budgeted Do runs (same start path as scheduled runs), calls a judge through inference-core with the success criteria and the run's proof bundle and postcondition results, and updates the goal; renewable delegated credential so each continuation re-checks authority through the Control reauthorizer; goal bar and budget display in the Agent Run Console and the Work panel; cost reservation per continuation.
risks: Runaway cost (hard budget, per-continuation reservation); each continuation must re-verify authority; judge model can be gamed, so tie it to deterministic postconditions and the proof bundle where available; do not auto-continue across approval-required effects without a human.

verevon.exactGap: No Goal record, budget accounting, completion judge or continuation driver exists. The nearest primitives are an in-memory TeamWorker (objective, context, success_criteria, no budget or judge) in coordinator.rs, a run's plain goal string, deterministic postcondition verifiers for effects, and the scheduled-step lane, which is one tool-less, 1,024-token, tool_choice none inference per step (execution-core grpc.rs:498-523) and so cannot continue a Do run. A run ends when its rounds end (DEFAULT_MAX_ROUNDS 12) and its credentials lapse at the delegated bearer lifetime.
reuse: ScheduledRunSupervision and the per-fire Control authorization pattern (reauthorizeScheduleFire, AuthorizeScheduledStep) as the model for per-continuation authority
scheduled_inference_auth.rs service credential minting (narrow inference:invoke scope) if the judge runs service-side
postcondition.rs, verified_outcome.proto and proof_bundle.proto as deterministic completion evidence for effectful goals
RunDeadline in run_budget.rs and cost-core GetRunUsage for budget accounting
session-core Plan and Todo records and the Work panel for goal progress display
AgentRunConsole goal launcher and schedule-from-chat for the UI entry and "continue later"
verevon.constraints: Each continuation is unattended work, so it needs fresh Control-owned authorization; the only unattended lane today (model.schedule.step) is tool-less single-step and the workflow is marked DeniesZDR, and an unattended governed Do-run lane does not exist (plan D10 is an L, OD8 is the credential decision). A durable Goal row persists content, so ZDR threads must be refused (the item omits ZDR). Go workflow step responses carry no usage (the AutoresearchWorkflow exclusion in workflowreg.go says so), so token budget must come from cost-core run usage, and on the Subscription route nothing is metered so a token budget is a no-op. Never auto-continue across approval-required effects (ScheduledRunSupervision already fails on NeedsApproval). The judge call must inherit the turn privacy-tier floor.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not describe the driver as starting Do runs on "the same start path as scheduled runs": that lane executes one tool-less inference. Reframe as (1) a Goal record and budget ledger in session-core, non-ZDR only; (2) a continuation workflow modelled on ScheduledRunSupervision that obtains fresh Control authorization per continuation and starts a governed RunAgent, which requires the unattended Do-run lane (D10 and OD8) first; (3) a judge that prefers the proof bundle and postcondition results and falls back to a rubric judge through inference-core. A smaller attended first slice is possible: a goal bar in the Agent Run Console that auto-continues while the user session still holds delegated authority, with no new credential class.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from L: new durable record, a new unattended governed-run authority lane across Control and Model Plane, a judge, budget accounting from cost-core and the UI. L only for the attended first slice.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real and fully absent, but the premise that the scheduled lane can start budgeted Do runs is wrong and ZDR is missing from the constraints, so approach, dependencies and effort must change before it is planned.

verevon.verdictReason: Not shipped, but the item's premise that only a browser-side export exists is wrong (code_interpreter python-pptx is advertised and baked into the image) and plan H8 already plans the base deck path; the real delta is manifest, validation gate, present mode and template library, so the recommendation should be rewritten as that delta on top of H8.

title: Runtime release safety: signed candidate and separate rollback artifact, rehearsed rollback, deployed audit fix and a release gate
summary: Finish artifact format v3 end to end: build a signed candidate per release (image digests, migration set, compatibility gates) and a separate accepted rollback artifact, rehearse restoring it against a database snapshot, deploy the already-built audit publisher fix and replay the stuck rows, and gate deploys on a release-evidence check in coresystem-conformance.sh with numeric canary and rollback thresholds.
whyItMatters: Verevon cannot claim production readiness, or defend a ZDR and audit promise to enterprise buyers, without a reproducible signed release and a proven rollback. Postmortem 0002 shows the failure mode: a built fix sat undeployed while 4,992 audit events stayed stuck.

others: Claude desktop app (signed manifest, staged rollout)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: T3 installs the new version beside the old, preflights it, starts a trial child against a database snapshot and rolls back on failure. Claude ships a signed manifest {version, artifacts[sha256, size], compat} with staged rollout; Hermes restarts drain-first and keeps receipts for interrupted steps.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: SRC/DOC: artifact v3 tooling (11 services, pinned infrastructure images, refuses a dirty tree) and graceful drain exist, and the evidence register defines candidate and rollback evidence classes. The roadmap states no signed candidate or rollback artifact has been built, and postmortem 0002 (2026-10-06) records the audit publisher fix as built but not deployed. These docs are dated (the roadmap text also describes the approval dispatcher as missing although the worker now exists), so the current state needs a code-level re-check.

approachOriginal: Run artifact v3 in release mode with signing and verification keys; produce a separate rollback artifact from the prior revision; script a rollback rehearsal that restores the retained digest and runs the migration revert scripts against a snapshot; add a release-evidence check to coresystem-conformance.sh that fails when candidate or rollback evidence is missing; require forward-compatible (expand/contract) migrations; define canary thresholds and observation windows; deploy the session-core audit publisher fix and requeue the stuck rows.
planeOwner: Model Plane (release tooling), Infra Plane for deploy
risks: Rolling back Postgres migrations that changed data requires forward-compatible schemas; a rehearsal on production-shaped data is needed. Release gates can block urgent fixes without an emergency path.

title: Sandbox egress tiers and a credential-injecting egress proxy, with per-call enforcement reports and shell-grammar approvals
summary: Add an org and user network tier (off, package registries, allowlisted domains, all) stamped on the sandbox lease and mapped to the existing fail-closed MpNetworkPolicy, backed by a deployed egress proxy that injects vaulted credentials so sandboxes only ever see sentinels. verevon.constraints: Egress tiers are Control-owned policy (org and user level, tied to the F-t3-032 registry) carried in the Control-signed Space decision; Model Plane enforces and must stay fail-closed (unknown tier means Disabled). Today Control grants space:egress for any non-default egress claim with no org egress entitlement, contrary to its own design doc, so that must be fixed before tiers. ZDR: the capability decision is ZDR-compatible only because scratch is credential-free and egress-less; any tier above off must be refused or separately gated for ZDR and high-risk runs. Outbound fetching and the SSRF guard belong to Quarry (Ingestion Plane), so a sandbox proxy must reuse that guard instead of re-implementing it. A credential-injecting proxy needs a Control-held secret store; execution-core must never hold plaintext service credentials, and credential_mode is part of the signed claim, so a credentialed backend is a new claim and a new attested backend. Real enforcement needs a dedicated netns or firewall (or the F-t3-009 VM): bwrap with a shared network namespace plus HTTPS_PROXY only constrains cooperative clients.

Do not deploy a proxy and call AllowDomains enforced; add netns/firewall enforcement or defer to the VM backend, and reuse Quarry's dns_guard. Split: (a) S: add sandboxed/enforcement fields to CodeResult and process_* results from ExecOutcome and the measured profile, shown as a tool-card badge (useful now, while network is simply off); (b) L: tiers, allowlist proxy and namespace enforcement; (c) XL, demote: credential-injecting proxy (TLS interception CA in the sandbox, Control secret store, per-host re-signing); (d) M, separate: shell-grammar approvals; (e) versioned file writes belong to F-t3-030.

verevon.verdictReason: The fail-closed policy, signed egress claim and space:egress gating already exist, so the item should extend them instead of adding a lease key; the proxy as described is advisory under a shared network namespace; and the bundle should be split with the credential proxy demoted.

title: Sharing, replay, export and import: governed snapshot links, org-only default, and conversation export and import
summary: Add a session-core snapshot entity (owner, visibility org or named people, created_from_message) whose grants are checked through Control Plane and audited, with public links only behind admin policy and refused for ZDR threads and threads that used private connectors unless redacted. Viewers read it read-only and a follow-up creates a fork under the viewer; a replay view is built from the durable run event log. In parallel add an owner-only audited whole-conversation export and an importer that maps ChatGPT and Claude export JSON into origin=import threads.
whyItMatters: Teams share answers and agent runs constantly and org-only sharing is expected in B2B (8 of 12 sources). A replay of an agent run is also a strong trust and transparency artefact. Importing history lowers switching cost, and reports must leave Verevon as Office files and PDFs.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Manus (SRC) for visibility, roles, replay and admin policy; claude.ai and Perplexity (DOC) for snapshot hygiene and fork-on-follow-up; Manus (SRC) and Claude desktop (SRC) for conversion and import
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 8 of 12 for sharing (table-stakes); 6 of 12 for export and import (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Share is an immutable snapshot of the thread up to a message (artifacts included, raw tool and connector payloads and files excluded unless in-org) with a visibility enum and an audit entry. Viewers load read-only, a follow-up forks under the viewer, replay plays recorded steps with a countdown and skip-to-result, and admin policy can disable public or replay sharing (strictest wins). Export uses server-side conversion jobs with PENDING, CONVERTING, SUCCESS and FAILED states, session export as a zip (rate-limited, policy-gated), and importers that enumerate sources and can remove an import run.

verevonTodayOriginal.gap: No chat share link exists (status absent; deferred pending the owner's share-model ruling). Export is partly shipped: answers export to Word, Excel and PowerPoint and print-to-PDF in the browser with pure in-browser OOXML builders (no network, good for ZDR), but without images, charts or math, PDF goes through the print dialog, there is no whole-conversation or account export endpoint, and no importer from ChatGPT or Claude exports.

approachOriginal: session-core: a snapshot entity with a visibility enum and Control Plane grant and audit checks; the viewer follow-up reuses ForkThread from R-t3-01-02. sessions.proto already stores recipient_audience_revision and hash so share, replay and fork can detect a participant-set change. Replay is built from the durable run event log. Client builders stay and gain chart and image embedding (plan H3/H4); add a session-core export (owner-only, audited) and an importer that marks imported turns untrusted. Refuse sharing and import for ZDR threads, and honour admin policy.
planeOwner: Model Plane (snapshots, export, import), Control Plane (grants, audit, admin policy)
risks: Leakage of connector content, ZDR and residency violations, and legal retention of public snapshots. Imported content may carry prompt injections.

alreadyPlanned.where: Partly: plan I19 read-only share link (deferred to Wave 6, owner-gated, apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/verevon-web/plans/system-audits/CHAT_GAP_CLOSURE_PLAN_2026-10-01.md:271) and I20 copy a chat into a Space (:272); H3 direct PDF and H4 native charts in Office exports (Wave 4); backlog item #22 governed share and replay (apps/Model Plane/docs/verevon_CHAT_PARITY_BACKLOG.md:176); import and whole-conversation export are not planned

verevon.exactGap: Share link is absent: there is no chat share route, gateway shares.rs and user-core grants cover documents only, and user-core's taxonomy lists 'document' as the only ownable type and rejects any other type for a per-user grant, so a snapshot or thread grant needs a new classified type in Control Plane. Replay primitives exist (session-core ReplayThread, gateway GET /v1/threads/:id/events and /v1/runs/:id/events/replay) but are envelope-only or browser-agent projections by deliberate design, so a content-bearing replay needs a new redacted projection, and there is no ForkThread RPC (artifacts.rs fork_thread only forks artifact counters) and no 'import' value in session-core THREAD_ORIGINS. Export is partly shipped (per-answer Word, Excel, PowerPoint and print-to-PDF built in the browser via ChatMessages.tsx exportMenuItems) but there is no whole-conversation export (the DSAR export is Control-Plane-only by its own disclosure) and no ChatGPT or Claude importer.
reuse: session-core ReplayThread and the replay_run_events pattern (GetRun ownership proof first, then filter payloads before they leave the boundary)
sessions.proto recipient_audience_revision and recipient_audience_hash on threads, already documented as the share/replay/fork drift detector
user-core resource_grants facade plus authztaxonomy (extend with a new type) and the gateway shares.rs / ShareDialog pattern
chat-export docx/xlsx/pptx/zip builders and chatThreadHref deep-link helper
session audit outbox pattern (audit_publisher) for an audited export event
plan I19 (read-only share link), I20 (copy chat into a Space), I8 (server-owned branch conversation)
verevon.constraints: Threads are owned by session-core, so the snapshot entity belongs in Model Plane, but grants and admin policy must be Control Plane authority: add a new resource type to user-core's resource_taxonomy.json (the Go embed, the retrieval-engine-rs mirror and the lint script must stay in parity) rather than any Model Plane-local ACL; Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL. ZDR threads have no durable transcript (persistence-free execution) so sharing, replay and export must refuse them, and connector or private-connector content must be redacted or refused. The existing replay routes are deliberately not browser-safe (gateway comment: payloads may carry prompt, provider or connector data), so replay must be a new redacted projection, not a pass-through of the event log. Import needs a new origin value in THREAD_ORIGINS and the DB CHECK constraint, and imported turns must be marked untrusted because they can carry prompt injections.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Drop the claim that the viewer follow-up reuses ForkThread: no such RPC exists, so either land plan I8/I20 first or ship the first release view-only. Build the share as an immutable redacted snapshot copy (OD19 recommends an org-internal sign-in link, 30-day expiry, revocable, redacted text view) rather than a live view of the thread, and do not describe replay as 'built from the durable run event log' because that log is envelope-only today. Split export and import into an owner-only track that needs no share-model ruling.
verevon.effortNote: Bundles a snapshot entity with Control grants and redaction, a new redacted replay projection, whole-conversation export, an importer and a fork dependency. Recommend splitting: share snapshot L (owner-gated by OD19, plan Wave 6 says do not start), export M, import M.
verevon.verdictReason: Share is correctly missing but already planned and owner-gated (I19), the replay premise is wrong as stated (event logs are envelope-only by design), ForkThread does not exist, and export is partly shipped; the item should be split and its dependencies corrected.

title: Event-triggered automations: normalised connector events from Ingestion wake budgeted runs, with wake gates, dry runs, blueprints and consent-first suggestions
summary: Add trigger records in capability-core (provider event, structured filter plus optional LLM predicate, prompt template, run target, revision, dry-run) subscribed to normalised events that integration-corev2 publishes on NATS, starting budgeted Do runs through the scheduled-run path with wake gates (source-hash, silent sentinel), per-automation notes, blueprints and capped, de-duplicated suggestions.
whyItMatters: Event triggers are common (5 of 12): Cursor's automations service and Hermes's wake gates are the references, ChatGPT MCP Events the DOC-level variant. They turn Verevon agents from on-demand into proactive, which is the natural next step after scheduled runs.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Cursor (automations service with event triggers, LLM filtering and dry runs) for triggers; Hermes (source-hash wake gate, silent sentinel, per-job notepad, blueprints, suggestions with a dedup latch and cap of 5) for state and authoring ; ChatGPT MCP Events (web-chatgpt-web-product-044, DOC)
others: Manus (trigger catalog with revisions, dry runs and execution history; AI triage of failed runs)
web ChatGPT (task definitions shared as independent copies)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: R-t3-04-07: event triggers 5 of 12 (common); wake gates 3 of 12; authoring and sharing 3 of 12; proactive suggestions 3 of 12 | R-t3-03-12: 1 of 11 sources; unique (DOC only)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Trigger{source, filter, prompt template, run_target, revision}; The server declares an events capability, the client subscribes with a callback URL and signing secret, the provider posts signed webhooks (Standard Webhooks HMAC, 256 KiB cap), the receiver verifies, batches events and starts a task run in the bound conversation.

approachOriginal: Ingestion owns provider webhooks and normalisation; Model Plane owns triggers and runs; reuse the unattended contract of F-t3-018.
planeOwner: Model Plane (capability-core triggers) with Ingestion Plane (integration-corev2 events)
risks: Event storms and cost; unattended authority; prompt injection through event payloads.

verevon.exactGap: No connector-event trigger exists: integration-corev2 publishes verevon.ingestion.integration.webhook_received (server.go:1080) carrying only eventType, webhookEventId and normalizedBy while the payload stays in its own store, and the only consumer found is Application Plane conversation-core; Model Plane has no consumer for it. capability-core has time-based cron_schedules with a per-fire FireAuthorizer, a Watch primitive with a single process_output adapter and an explicit one-resource-one-Space-one-member authority model, and a run-finished notifier, but no trigger records, structured or LLM filters, wake gates, dry runs or blueprints; chat only offers a time-based "Schedule this" dialog. The webhook normaliser derives just an event type, ids and a replay key, so filters would run over raw provider JSON.
evidence: apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2/internal/api/server.go:1050-1100 (publishes webhook_received after storing the payload; data = eventType, webhookEventId, normalizedBy)

reuse: cron_schedules + Sweeper + FireAuthorizer/FireIntent + cron_fires as the template for a trigger row, per-fire reauthorization and run history
Watch primitive (cursor, dedupe, expiry, trust column, summary bound) as the home of a new connector-event source kind
conversation-core webhook_received consumer (durable JetStream + FetchWebhookEvent by webhookEventId) as the consumption pattern
runwatch / sessionreview JetStream consumers in capability-core for ack and redelivery behaviour
Scheduled-run path (PrepareScheduledRunThread, orchestrator StartScheduledRunActivity) for starting the budgeted Do run
Run budget and org quota machinery (run_budget.rs, org_quota.rs) for the per-automation cap
verevon.constraints: Ingestion owns provider webhooks and normalisation; Model Plane owns triggers and runs; no cross-plane DB access, so the payload must be fetched through integration-corev2 API (as conversation-core does), not read from its tables. Authority: a trigger must be bound to one connection, Space and acting member and reauthorized with a fresh Control decision on every fire, because the Watch primitive deliberately refuses org-wide subscriptions and a stored record is not authority. Event payloads are attacker-influenced untrusted content (prompt injection) and must be classified untrusted before any LLM predicate or run. ZDR must come from policy because there is no user turn, and unattended runs have no precedent outside Space-scoped scheduled runs (mail_task.rs). A new JetStream durable needs a nats-provisioner binding; event storms need rate limits and budgets.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Model a trigger as a new Watch source kind or a cron_schedules-like row keyed by (connection_id, Space, member) that implements FireAuthorizer, not as free-standing org-wide subscriptions in capability-core. Consume webhook_received through a durable JetStream consumer, fetch the payload by webhookEventId, dedupe on it as the fire key, and treat the payload as untrusted_source_payload. State honestly that integration-corev2 publishes only three event types in code (webhook_received, scim_event_received, sync_cancelled; INF by pattern search) and no mail-received event, so useful mail triggers need an Ingestion-side change first.
verevon.effortNote: As written (trigger store, consumer, filters plus LLM predicate, wake gates, dry run, blueprints, suggestions, unattended Space-authority runs, UI) it is XL; trimmed to trigger + consumer + wake gate + budgeted run it is L, with blueprints and suggestions deferred.
verevon.verdictReason: Confirmed absent in code, with a clear existing pattern to build on. Keep, but reshape around the Watch and FireAuthorizer authority model, flag the missing event types, and trim scope.
